subject: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moss <elena.moss@acme.com>; procurement@acme.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request

Hi Elena / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I ran the numbers for a 3-year commitment with an annual prepay structure and a modest term discount tied to the upfront commitment. High-level, the proposal I attached includes: 

- 3-year term (annual invoicing) with an overall 16% term discount vs list for the committed units across the term.
- Year 1: 60% upfront prepay for that year to support onboarding, dedicated pool reservation, and initial support SLAs.
- Year 2 & 3: 40% invoice for the year issued Net90 from invoice date (this is the exception you asked us to consider).
- Accelerator credit: $50k one-time deployment credit applied against the first-year invoice if you elect the annual prepay.

I know Jake flagged internal cashflow constraints; the split above is an attempt to balance their request for longer payment windows with our need for predictable capacity commitments. If Acme prefers a milestone schedule instead of straight Net90 for Y2/Y3 (e.g., 25% at the start of the year / 15% at mid-year), we can model that too.

Attached: SOW draft and an invoice schedule workbook with line-level timing. Please confirm whether finance would sign off on Net90 for the non-upfront portion or if we should propose Net60 for year 2 as a compromise.

Next steps: if the economics look good, I can pull Marissa in to finalize pricing and have our finance team draft the billing amendment and DocuSign packet.

Thanks,

— Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0104

Attachments (3): ACME_Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), InvoiceSchedule_ACME.xlsx (Excel, 64KB), redwood_pricing_sheet_q4_2026.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)
From: Elena Moss <elena.moss@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Doe <j.doe@acme.com>; procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request

Logan —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the workbook. A few notes from finance / procurement after internal sync: 

1) We can accept a material upfront (we prefer front-loading to avoid capacity risk) but cannot do 60% in year 1 — 40% is about the max we can secure in Q1 without board approval.
2) Net90 on the remaining annual balance is doable but only if we have a signed SOW and a milestone acceptance schedule tied to feature delivery and uptime SLAs.
3) The $50k accelerator credit is appreciated — procurement would prefer that as a line-item credit rather than a rebate to simplify accounting.

Can you produce a revised schedule with: 40% Y1 upfront, 30% at start of Y2 (invoice Net90), 30% at start of Y3 (invoice Net90), and an acceptance milestone matrix? If Redwood can include a soft SLO around onboarding completion (target: 8 weeks), that will help.

Elena
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Robotics

Date: 2026-10-23T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request

Elena —

Appreciate the quick review and the specifics. We can do the 40/30/30 split you requested. A few clarifications and things we should lock down before I send the formal amendment:

- Term discount: to preserve the economics for Redwood and the reserved capacity model, the 16% term discount scales down to 13% if Acme reduces the Y1 prepay below 50%. With the 40% upfront ask, we can offer 14% discount.
- Acceptance milestones: we will add an onboarding milestone ("Onboarding complete — KV cache warm & first production load") targeted at 8 weeks, and an availability milestone at 99.5% over the first 90 days tied to the milestone payment.
- Invoice timing: Y2/Y3 invoices will be issued with Net90 payment terms. For accounting ease we'll put the accelerator credit as a distinct line credit applied to the first invoice.

Marissa / Ben / Priyom — can you review the revised pricing matrix and confirm the discount ladder (14% at 40% upfront, 16% at >=50% upfront)? Also confirming that finance is comfortable with issuing Y2/Y3 invoices Net90 as long as the SOW includes the milestone acceptance criteria.

If everyone is aligned I'll prepare a one-page billing amendment and route it to DocuSign.

— Logan

On Oct 22, 2026, at 11:05 AM, Elena Moss <elena.moss@acme.com> wrote:

Date: 2026-10-23T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request

Thanks Logan — quick note from pricing: the discount ladder you've proposed is OK but we need to tighten the kicker that preserves unit economics for reserved GPU pools. Specifically: 

- 14% at 40% upfront is acceptable if Acme commits to a utilization floor (70% of committed units over a trailing 30-day period) or agrees to a small reserved-capacity true-up.
- Otherwise we need to keep 16% but require 50%+ upfront.

Ben — can you flag if that reserve/true-up logic is workable operationally? Priyom — heads-up that legal may want tighter language around the milestone acceptance and refund/credit mechanics.

Marissa
Head of Pricing
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-24T15:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request

Marissa — operationally we can support a utilization floor clause. A suggested fallback: if utilization < 70% for two consecutive months we automatically trigger a credit calculation and apply it against the next invoice; that keeps the accounting tidy and avoids monthly reconciliations. We can document that in the SOW.

Logan — on the billing side, finance is okay to issue Y2/Y3 invoices Net90 provided we receive an executed amendment and the milestone confirmation email from Acme's product lead. We should make sure Acme understands billing won't begin for Y2 until the year-1 onboarding milestone is accepted.

Ben
VP, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Jake Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Elena Moss <elena.moss@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-12T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request

Logan / team —

We've reviewed the revised schedule internally. A couple of asks before we sign: 

1) Can Redwood reduce the term discount to 12% if we accept a 45% Y1 upfront instead of 40%? That gets our CFO comfortable and doesn't force immediate board approval.
2) We need plain-English billing flow in the SOW: when the Y2 invoice is raised (start of year 2), what evidence of milestone acceptance is required from Acme and what is Redwood's window to dispute an acceptance?

If you can send a final amendment with the 45%/30%/25% split and clarify acceptance windows, we can push to sign this month.

— Jake
VP Engineering, Acme Robotics
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Jake Doe <j.doe@acme.com>, Elena Moss <elena.moss@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Annual prepay + multi-year term: proposed split-invoice plan and Net90 exception request

Jake / Elena —

Thanks — attached is the final one-page billing amendment and a clean invoice timing table: 

- Split: Year1 45% upfront, Year2 30% (Net90), Year3 25% (Net90).
- Discount: 12% term discount tied to the 45% upfront. If Acme increases to >=50% upfront the discount steps to 15%.
- Accelerator credit: $50k shown as an invoice line credit on the Year1 invoice.
- Utilization floor: 70% utilization over any trailing 30-day window; if not met for two consecutive months, Redwood will calculate a pro rata credit applied to the next invoice.
- Acceptance windows: Acme to confirm onboarding acceptance within 14 days of Redwood providing the "Onboarding complete" checklist; absence of written dispute within 14 days will be treated as acceptance for invoicing purposes. Redwood will have 7 days to raise any billing disputes once an acceptance email is received.

If this looks good I'll send the amendment to DocuSign. Appreciate the flexibility from both teams to land on a path that balances capacity reservation and Acme's cashflow.

— Logan

Attachments (2): ACME_Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, final), InvoiceSchedule_ACME.xlsx (Excel)
